next_state_election.name: State General Election
next_state_election.source_name: Minnesota Secretary of State — Election Day Voting

glance_notes.source_name: Minnesota Secretary of State — Common Registration Questions
glance_notes.text: Advance Registration Deadline: Minnesota's advance voter registration deadline for the November 3, 2026 State General Election is October 13, 2026. Eligible voters who miss that deadline can still register at their polling place on Election Day.

glance_notes.source_name: Minnesota Secretary of State — Other Ways to Vote
glance_notes.text: Absentee Voting Begins September 18: Any eligible Minnesota voter may vote absentee without providing an excuse. Absentee ballots for the November 3, 2026 General Election are available beginning September 18 for voting by mail and in person.

glance_notes.source_name: Minnesota Secretary of State — Register on Election Day
glance_notes.text: Election Day Registration: Minnesota allows eligible residents to register or update their registration at their polling place on Election Day. Election Day registrants must provide an approved form of proof of residence.

register.label: Register to Vote
register.content: Eligible Minnesota residents may register online, by mail or on paper before the advance registration deadline, or register in person when voting on Election Day. To vote in Minnesota, a person must be a U.S. citizen, be at least 18 years old on Election Day, have maintained residence in Minnesota for at least 20 days immediately before Election Day, and maintain residence at the address used for voting. Minnesota allows eligible residents who are at least 16 years old to preregister. A person with a felony conviction may vote once the person is no longer incarcerated for the felony offense.
register.glance_value: Register in advance or on Election Day
register.source_name: Minnesota Secretary of State — Register to Vote
register.internal_note: Minnesota permits preregistration beginning at age 16. The state's felony-voting rule changed in 2023: voting rights are restored upon release from incarceration, including while a person remains on probation, supervised release or other community supervision. Do not use older descriptions requiring completion of the entire felony sentence.

check_registration.label: Check Voter Registration
check_registration.content: Use the Minnesota Secretary of State's official voter registration lookup to check whether your registration is current. Voters who have moved or changed their name should update their registration. If your registration is not current before Election Day, Minnesota allows you to register or update it at your polling place on Election Day with proof of residence.
check_registration.source_name: Minnesota Secretary of State — Voter Registration Status
check_registration.internal_note: Minnesota maintains a voter-status lookup through MNVotes. Election Day registration provides a fallback for eligible residents whose registration is missing or outdated.

deadlines.label: Registration Deadlines
deadlines.content: The advance registration deadline for Minnesota's November 3, 2026 General Election is October 13, 2026, which is 21 days before Election Day. Online registration must be submitted by 11:59 p.m. on the advance deadline. Eligible residents who miss advance registration may register or update their registration at their polling place on Election Day by providing approved proof of residence.
deadlines.source_name: Minnesota Secretary of State — Common Registration Questions
deadlines.internal_note: The Secretary of State directly states that online registration closes at 11:59 p.m. 21 days before Election Day. For November 3, 2026, that date is October 13. Minnesota Statutes section 201.061 expressly authorizes Election Day registration and registration updates with proof of residence.

polling_place.label: Find a Polling Place
polling_place.content: Use Minnesota's official Polling Place Finder to locate your assigned Election Day polling place. Polling locations are based on the address where you maintain residence. Because polling locations can change, voters should check the official finder before Election Day.
polling_place.source_name: Minnesota Secretary of State — Polling Place Finder
polling_place.internal_note: The Polling Place Finder is the Secretary of State's official address-based tool for Election Day polling locations. The state advises voters to verify their location because polling places can change.

election_day.label: Election Day Voting
election_day.content: Minnesota's State General Election is Tuesday, November 3, 2026. Polling places are generally open from 7:00 a.m. until 8:00 p.m. Some towns with fewer than 500 residents may legally open later, but no later than 10:00 a.m. Voters should verify their polling place and opening time before voting. Anyone who is in line by 8:00 p.m. is allowed to vote. A voter whose registration is current and active generally does not need to show identification. Eligible residents may also register or update their registration at the polling place on Election Day with proof of residence.
election_day.glance_value: Usually 7:00 a.m. – 8:00 p.m.; verify local opening time
election_day.source_name: Minnesota Secretary of State — Voting Hours
election_day.internal_note: Important Minnesota exception: do not state that every polling place opens at 7:00 a.m. Minnesota Statutes section 204C.05 allows qualifying towns with fewer than 500 residents outside the metropolitan area to establish a later opening time, no later than 10:00 a.m. The Secretary of State maintains a current list of towns opening later. All state and federal election polling places close at 8:00 p.m., and voters in line at 8:00 p.m. may vote.

polling_hours.label: Polling Hours
polling_hours.content: For Minnesota state and federal elections, polling places are usually open from 7:00 a.m. until 8:00 p.m. A qualifying town with fewer than 500 residents may establish a later opening time, but it cannot be later than 10:00 a.m. Most qualifying towns still open at 7:00 a.m. All polling places close at 8:00 p.m., and anyone in line by 8:00 p.m. may vote.
polling_hours.source_name: Minnesota Secretary of State — Voting Hours
polling_hours.internal_note: The Secretary of State's current page expressly states the 7:00 a.m.-8:00 p.m. general rule and the small-town exception. Minnesota Statutes section 204C.05 confirms that a qualifying organized town with fewer than 500 inhabitants outside the metropolitan area may establish an opening time as late as 10:00 a.m. after approval by town electors.

early_voting.label: Early In-Person Voting
early_voting.content: Minnesota allows any eligible voter to vote in person before Election Day without providing an excuse. Absentee in-person voting for the November 3, 2026 General Election begins September 18. Beginning October 16, Minnesota's early-voting process allows voters at participating locations to place completed ballots directly into a ballot counter before Election Day. The last day to vote early in person is Monday, November 2. Locations and hours vary, and designated locations have required extended hours on certain days before the election.
early_voting.source_name: Minnesota Secretary of State — Other Ways to Vote
early_voting.internal_note: Minnesota now distinguishes the broader 46-day absentee-voting period from statutory Early Voting. For the 2026 General Election, absentee ballots become available September 18, while Early Voting begins October 16 and allows ballots to be inserted directly into a ballot counter. The Secretary of State's voting-locations page lists November 2 as the final day to vote early in person. Do not describe October 16 as the beginning of all in-person pre-Election-Day voting because in-person absentee voting begins September 18.

absentee_mail.label: Absentee Voting by Mail
absentee_mail.content: Any eligible Minnesota voter may vote absentee without providing an excuse. For the November 3, 2026 General Election, absentee ballots become available September 18. Voters may apply for an absentee ballot online or by submitting a paper application to their county election office. Completed ordinary absentee ballots must be received by Election Day to be counted. Because mailing time can vary, voters should return ballots well before Election Day or use another authorized return method. Minnesota also offers a permanent absentee voter list for voters who want an absentee ballot sent automatically for elections for which they are eligible.
absentee_mail.glance_value: No excuse required; ballots available September 18
absentee_mail.source_name: Minnesota Secretary of State — Other Ways to Vote
absentee_mail.internal_note: The Secretary of State directly identifies September 18 as the first day absentee ballots are available for the 2026 General Election and November 3 as the ballot receipt deadline. Minnesota provides no-excuse absentee voting and a permanent absentee list. Military and overseas voters have separate procedures and should use the UOCAVA rules rather than relying solely on ordinary domestic absentee instructions.

voter_id.label: Voter ID Requirements
voter_id.content: A Minnesota voter whose registration is current and active generally does not need to show identification at the polling place. Identification or other proof of residence is required when registering or updating a registration at the polling place, and may also be required when a voter's registration is not active. Minnesota accepts several methods of proving residence for Election Day registration, including an approved identification document showing the current name and address, an approved photo ID combined with an accepted document showing the current name and address, and other methods authorized by state law.
voter_id.glance_value: No ID for most currently registered voters
voter_id.source_name: Minnesota Secretary of State — Do I Need to Bring ID?
voter_id.internal_note: Minnesota does not have a universal photo-ID-at-the-polls requirement. The Secretary of State directly states that voters whose registration is current and active do not need identification. Election Day registration requires proof of residence. Minnesota provides several proof methods, including current-address ID, photo ID plus an approved residence document, registered-voter vouching and specialized procedures for residential facilities and college students.

accessible_voting.label: Accessible Voting
accessible_voting.content: Minnesota provides accessible polling places, voting assistance and ballot-marking equipment for voters with disabilities. A voter may ask election judges for help or bring someone to assist with voting, subject to applicable restrictions. Accessible ballot-marking machines allow voters to mark a ballot privately using features such as audio instructions and alternative controls. Additional options may be available for voters who cannot easily enter a polling place or who live in certain residential or health-care facilities.
accessible_voting.glance_value: Accessible locations, assistance and ballot-marking machines
accessible_voting.source_name: Minnesota Secretary of State — Election Day Voting
accessible_voting.internal_note: The Secretary of State maintains separate official guidance for voter assistance, polling-place accessibility and ballot-marking machines under its Election Day Voting resources. Minnesota also has specialized absentee and agent-delivery procedures for voters in certain circumstances.

military_overseas.label: Military & Overseas Voting
military_overseas.content: Minnesota provides special absentee-voting procedures for eligible members of the Uniformed Services, their eligible spouses and dependents, Merchant Marine members, certain military-academy students and U.S. citizens living outside the United States. Covered voters may use Minnesota's online military and overseas absentee application or the Federal Post Card Application to request a ballot. Ballots may be delivered electronically when requested, but completed ballots must be returned using an authorized method under Minnesota's military and overseas voting rules. Eligible voters may also use the Federal Write-In Absentee Ballot as a backup when necessary.
military_overseas.glance_value: FPCA, electronic delivery and FWAB available
military_overseas.source_name: Minnesota Secretary of State — Military and Overseas Absentee Voting
military_overseas.internal_note: The current MNVotes UOCAVA application identifies active Uniformed Services and Merchant Marine members, eligible spouses and dependents, military-academy students and U.S. citizens residing abroad. Minnesota's election-administration materials contain separate instructions for electronically transmitted and mailed UOCAVA ballots. Avoid applying ordinary domestic absentee procedures to UOCAVA voters without checking the specific military/overseas rules.

student_voting.label: College / Student Voting
student_voting.content: College students may register in Minnesota using the address where they currently consider their home and intend to return after temporary absences. A student living on campus may use a campus residence as the voting address if it meets Minnesota's residence requirements. Students registering on Election Day have several ways to prove residence, including a Minnesota college or university photo ID combined with an approved document showing the current address. Colleges and universities may also provide residential housing lists that can help eligible students establish residence for Election Day registration.
student_voting.glance_value: Students may register at a qualifying campus residence
student_voting.source_name: Minnesota Secretary of State — Register on Election Day
student_voting.internal_note: Minnesota's Election Day registration rules expressly accept Minnesota university, college and technical-college IDs as approved photo identification when combined with an accepted current-address document. State law also provides specialized student-residence proof procedures. The reader-facing text does not imply that simply attending a Minnesota school automatically establishes voting residence.

sample_ballot.label: Official Sample Ballot
sample_ballot.content: Minnesota voters can use the Secretary of State's official sample-ballot service to view the candidates and questions expected to appear on their ballot when information for the election is available. Because ballot contents depend on the voter's address, precinct and electoral districts, voters should use their residential address to obtain the sample ballot that applies to them.
sample_ballot.glance_value: View your ballot through the state sample-ballot tool
sample_ballot.source_name: Minnesota Secretary of State — My Ballot
sample_ballot.internal_note: My Ballot is Minnesota's official voter-specific sample-ballot service. General Election ballot information continues to develop after the primary and candidate-certification process, so this section should be reverified closer to November.

contact.label: Contact the State Election Authority
contact.content: Minnesota Secretary of State, Elections & Administration, Veterans Service Building, Suite 210, 20 W 12th Street, Saint Paul, MN 55155. Metro Area phone: 651-215-1440. Greater Minnesota: 1-877-600-VOTE (8683). Minnesota Relay Service: 711. Elections text/SMS: 651-217-3862. Email: secretary.state@state.mn.us. Regular office hours are 8:00 a.m. to 4:00 p.m. The Veterans Service Building has limited public access, so people who need in-person service should arrange it in advance. County election offices can assist with voter-specific registration, absentee-ballot and polling-place questions.
contact.source_name: Minnesota Secretary of State — Elections & Voting
contact.internal_note: The Secretary of State's current election pages directly verify the Veterans Service Building address, 651-215-1440 metro number, 1-877-600-VOTE Greater Minnesota number, 711 Relay Service, 651-217-3862 elections text number, [secretary.state@state.mn.us](mailto:secretary.state@state.mn.us) email and 8:00 a.m.-4:00 p.m. hours. The email address is intentionally plain text with no Markdown or mailto syntax.

official_resources.label: Official State & Local Resources
official_resources.content: Use the Minnesota Secretary of State Elections & Voting website for official statewide election information. The state's online voter services provide registration status, voter registration, polling-place lookup, sample ballots, absentee-ballot applications and ballot tracking. County election offices and municipal clerks administer many local election functions and can provide voter-specific assistance.
